comparator.name: History
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–2027 programme-specific Teaching and Examination Regulations establish a 180-EC History bachelor. Year 1 is 60 EC: A Global History of the Netherlands (5), Ancient World (5), Middle Ages (5), Making of the Modern World 1500–1945 (10), Long 20th Century (10), Historical Research (10), Regions: Introduction (5), and an IMPACT course in Global Changes or Cultural Heritage (10). Year 2 is 60 EC: Sources and Methods (10), three 10-EC research seminars in Political, Cultural, and Social-economic History, Historiography (5), Historical Theory (5), and Regions: Research Seminar (10). Year 3 is a 30-EC minor, Theory of History in Practice (5), Regions: Case Studies (10), Workshop Public History (5), and BA Thesis (10). The published structure therefore accounts for 60 + 60 + 60 = 180 EC without inventing elective content.

core: Regional and global history from the ancient world through the present, including Dutch history in global context
Connections between the historical past and present political, social and cultural questions
Political, cultural, economic and social history as explicit disciplinary directions
Historical evidence, source criticism, methods, historiography, theory, interpretation and debate
Regional research, historical writing and independent thesis research
Public history, cultural heritage and communicating historical change beyond the university
adjacent: Political culture, international order, conflict and institutions in historical perspective
Economic and social history, inequality, organisations and long-run change
Cultural history, identity, representation, heritage and public memory
Global change as an interdisciplinary history theme
questions: How do historical developments connect the past to present political, social, economic and cultural questions?
How can historical sources and interpretations be analysed critically and used as evidence?
How have regions, empires, institutions, conflict, inequality and cultural identities changed across periods?

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the generic historical identity, the full six-course UCR History sequence, methods and public-facing cultural history. Groningen formally includes three distinct 10-EC research seminars in Political, Cultural, and Social-economic History. Cultural History is integrated into the closest match; Political History and Social-economic History support two additional feasible directions. All three retain the complete UCR History sequence but diverge substantially in adjacent courses. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

alternatives.label: History, culture & public memory
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines every available UCR History course with archaeology, art history, sociology, heritage, literature, media and historical writing. It is the closest feasible response to Groningen’s broad chronological curriculum and formal Cultural History direction, without implying that UCR offers a full History major.
alternatives.concept: A broad historical route connecting the full UCR History sequence with archaeology, ancient and Mediterranean worlds, art and religion, social change, heritage, museums, literature, race, documentary practice and public historical communication.
progression: Modern History, sociology and Western art history establish chronological, social and visual foundations in semester 1. Histories of Gender, the history of warfare and the Renaissance Mediterranean precede work on empire, modern sociology, Indigenous histories, African heritage and world archaeology. The final year concentrates advanced social theory, museums, race, film, art-historical writing, documentary practice and the History Research Seminar. Every course is available in its assigned term and all formal prerequisites are satisfied.

alternatives.label: History, politics & conflict
alternatives.labelReason: The route retains all six UCR History courses while concentrating its adjacent work in comparative politics, international relations, conflict, international and EU law, institutions and political culture. It is the feasible UCR response to Groningen’s formal Political History direction.
alternatives.concept: A political-history route linking modern history, empire, warfare, gender and Indigenous histories with comparative politics, international-relations theory, conflict and peace, human rights, international and EU law, sociology, race, media and public argument.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces most archaeology, art, heritage, literature and media work with law, comparative politics, international relations, EU politics and Peace & Conflict. Its organising question moves from cultural history and public memory to political institutions, conflict and power.
progression: Modern History, Law, Society & Justice and comparative politics establish the historical, legal and political foundations in semester 1. Law, Society & Justice precedes all selected later law courses that formally require it. Survey History and international-relations theory precede the advanced work in empire, warfare, international law, constitutional comparison, conflict, EU law and EU politics conceptually. Native American Histories, advanced social theory and the final History Research Seminar deepen independent analysis. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: History, economy & society
alternatives.labelReason: The route retains the complete UCR History sequence and adds economics, sociology, political institutions, quantitative and qualitative methods, organisations and public communication. It is the feasible UCR response to Groningen’s formal Social-economic History direction.
alternatives.concept: A social-economic history route connecting the complete UCR History sequence to long-run growth, crises, markets, public policy, inequality, institutions, sociology, research methods and public historical communication.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes the archaeology, art, heritage, literature and media concentration and adds economics, econometrics, quantitative methods, political institutions and organisational psychology. Its organising logic is inequality, capitalism, crises and social-economic change rather than cultural history and public memory.
progression: Modern History, introductory economics and sociology establish the historical, economic and social foundations in semester 1. Research Methods & Statistics precedes every selected economics course that formally requires it. Survey and thematic History courses lead to Native American Histories and the final History Research Seminar. The final semesters integrate advanced economics, econometrics, behaviour, institutions and public rhetoric. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed earlier.

blocks: Historical periods, comparison & regional and global coverage
Both survey modern and contemporary political, social and cultural change; UCR begins in 1815 and is less specifically European.
Both examine historical power and identity across long periods; UCR does so comparatively through empires rather than the programme's broader chronological and regional sequence.

UCR's history of warfare contributes a comparative research-based account of changing power, states and conflict; the Groningen seminar has a broader ancient and medieval regional and global History scope.

Introduction to World Archaeology uses artefacts and material culture to study ancient societies across world regions; Groningen's course is dedicated ancient history and therefore has greater period-specific historical depth.

Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean covers a substantial early-modern European and Mediterranean segment through art, trade and cross-cultural exchange; it is not a full early-modern history survey.
Western art history includes urban, civic and cultural contexts relevant to cities and citizens, but does not reproduce Groningen's dedicated ancient and medieval history course.
UCR has no scheduled course providing the dedicated medieval-history breadth and weight of Groningen's compulsory course.
Historical methods, data, writing & independent inquiry
Research Methods & Statistics supplies research design and quantitative analysis relevant to big-data historical questions, but is not taught as a dedicated digital-history course.
Both teach systematic source collection, interpretation and reflexivity; Groningen applies these skills specifically in a historical research laboratory.
Both develop structured academic argument, evidence use and writing; Groningen's course is specifically historical writing.
Writing Art's Histories explicitly studies historiography and the interpretation of historical scholarship, within art history rather than the full history discipline.
History Research Seminar is UCR's closest scheduled independent historical-research experience and culminates in a substantial paper; it is 7.5 EC and not Groningen's required 10-EC bachelor thesis.
UCR History courses provide comparative and global perspectives, but no scheduled course reproduces the dedicated survey of Dutch history in global context.
UCR courses provide philosophical and social context, but no scheduled course is a dedicated foundations-of-history requirement at Groningen's specified scope.
Groningen's 30-EC minor or approved study-abroad package is genuine open profiling space; no single content is invented or equated to one UCR course.
Groningen preserves a bounded 10-EC choice between Global Changes and Cultural Heritage; no single option is invented or equated to one UCR course.
UCR embeds regional cases across its History courses but has no separate introductory regional-history requirement.
UCR can assemble social and economic history through History, sociology and economics, but it has no dedicated 10-EC Social-economic History research seminar.
UCR uses regional case studies within several courses but has no dedicated 10-EC Regions III course.
Heritage, museums, documentary work and communication support public history, but UCR has no dedicated compulsory Public History workshop.

notes.text: Groningen’s programme is a coherent 180-EC History degree with chronological coverage from the ancient world through the present, compulsory political, cultural and social-economic research seminars, historical methods, theory and historiography, regional research, public history and a BA thesis. UCR offers six History courses and can build strong historical pathways with archaeology, economics, politics, sociology, law, heritage, literature and media, but it does not reproduce that continuous disciplinary sequence or its full research and thesis requirements. These pathways are close or related liberal-arts responses, not substitutes for a full History major.
